why: The obvious "make PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE an override" edit, which prerequisites.test.ts already names in prose as this case's negative control. PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE is a PREFERENCE, not an override: a stale or mistyped value must not stop capture from finding a working install, and the aggregate failure must list every specifier it tried. Under the mutation a contributor whose PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE points at a moved install is told "Playwright with Chromium is required" with only that one dead path under `Tried:`, while a perfectly good ambient `playwright` is never attempted. MOVED for issue #692: the candidate order used to be a line inside prerequisites.mjs's `loadPlaywright`; it is now `playwrightCandidates` in tools/shared/playwright.mjs, which `loadPlaywright` and every other tool's loader call, so the same mutation now reaches all of them and the entry scopes the shared loader's tests beside capture's. Killed in capture by `treats PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE as the first candidate and still tries the bare specifier` (#353), the only capture case that reads the second `Tried:` line; in the shared loader by the candidate-order case, the fall-through case (the bare specifier is never asked for), and the aggregate-error case (its `playwright:` line is missing). Measured in both worlds this repo actually runs in, because Playwright is deliberately not a declared dependency: with node_modules/playwright{,-core} present (the documented local capture setup) and with them absent (CI's `verify` job, which installs Playwright only in the separate `visual` job). The capture assertion's second `Tried:` line's TEXT differs between them; the line is PRESENT either way, and the shared loader's cases never let the bare specifier reach this machine's resolver.
killedBy: capture prerequisites treats PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE as the first candidate and still tries the bare specifier
shared playwright loader tries PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE first and the bare specifier second, each once
